messages:
maya_releaselead: deploy-bot just flagged a canary regression in eu-west-1 :rotating_light: 

deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary traffic 12:05 UTC — p95 latency jump to 420ms (baseline 180ms), error-rate 2.7% (>2% threshold). Affected route: /v1/generate. Suggested action: evaluate rollback.

priya_sre: seeing the same in metrics, span traces show increased queue wait on the kv-cache layer. Noted a small increase in GPU OOM retries as well.

ben_release_engineer: any correlating infra deploys?

ryan_eng: no infra deploys in the last 2h. This came in with release 3.3.0 -> 3.4.0 rollout (canary 5%).

maya_releaselead: quick decision needed — customer-impacting threshold crossed. We can either let auto-rollback run (deploy-bot will revert if deploybot.auto_rollback=true) or do a manual targeted rollback / pin. Thoughts?

tom_pm: customer impact >2% errors on generate — I'd prefer manual rollback + pin for Hosted and Dedicated canaries. Comms: support and SRE should be notified.

priya_sre: agree. Automated rollback is fine normally but we've seen noisy p95 spikes since last patch; manual gives us control to capture traces and avoid oscillation. Recommend rollback to 3.3.1 (last good).

ben_release_engineer: ok — plan: 1) pause canary traffic 2) rollback canary -> 3.3.1 3) pin 3.3.1 for 30m on canary groups, hold further rollout 4) run smoke checks and gradually resume if green.

maya_releaselead: calling it: manual rollback to 3.3.1 and pin. @deploy-bot runbook: execute rollback to 3.3.1 for canary in eu-west-1 only. Also pin hosted route for 30m. @lucy_support please draft a short customer-facing note in #support-alerts.

deploy-bot: Received command. Suggested CLI: 
```
redwood deploy rollback --to-version=3.3.1 --scope=canary --region=eu-west-1 --reason="p95+error regression" --pin-duration=30m
```
Executing pause of traffic split now.

ben_release_engineer: running smoke tests after rollback — tailing logs: `tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/canary/eu-west-1.log`

ryan_eng: logs show immediate reduction in queue wait after rollback trigger.

deploy-bot: Rollback started at 2301234582. Canary traffic paused. Rolling back to 3.3.1 (artifact sha: a1b2c3d). Estimated completion 2m.

lucy_support: drafting customer blurb: "We detected and mitigated an issue affecting text generation latency for a subset of requests. We've rolled back a canary release and are monitoring. No customer action required." Will post once approved.

priya_sre: smoke checks ok so far (routes responding, p95 ~170ms, error-rate 0.4%). Keeping pin for 30m.

maya_releaselead: posting to #incidents and paging oncall for visibility. @tom_pm can you update release notes with a short rollback entry and link to traces?

tom_pm: done — added note to the release draft: "Hot rollback: 3.4.0 -> 3.3.1 due to p95 and error-rate regression observed in canary (eu-west-1). Investigating kv-cache queuing behavior."

deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 2301234599. Canary now on 3.3.1. Pin applied for 30m.

ben_release_engineer: verifying metrics dashboard — p95 back within baseline, error-rate normalized.

ryan_eng: captured traces and perf profiles from the canary window, saving to s3://redwood-debug/2301234567-canary-traces.tar.gz

maya_releaselead: great, thank you. Next steps: 1) postmortem in next 48h 2) hold rollout for further analysis 3) optional controlled re-roll with additional telemetry flags.

lucy_support: customer blurb posted in #support-alerts and sent to top 10 customers with active SLAs.

priya_sre: note for postmortem: include criteria that triggered manual vs auto-rollback decision (p95>300ms OR errors>2% for 5m), and recommend adding a secondary signal for KV-retry spikes.

maya_releaselead: copy. Closing this thread — if anyone sees re-emergence ping me. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ben_release_engineer: confirmed thread done, leaving monitoring.

deploy-bot: Incident note: manual rollback executed, pinned canary version. Logged action id: rb-2301234567-a1b2c3d.
